key_insight: Turbulent coherent structures are framed as universal thermodynamic responses to macroscopic energy-throughput imbalance, not as ad hoc flow features.
engineering_relevance: A computable order parameter (Π) could help decide which turbulent flows require finer resolution and better support predictive modeling in continuously driven systems.
method: Use renormalized Navier–Stokes equations to connect turbulence with non-equilibrium statistical physics.
Classify coherence as either near-equilibrium-like transient adjustments or far-from-equilibrium dissipative structures.
Define and compute an effective thermodynamic order parameter (Π) to identify required flow resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical framework and no numerical experiments or dataset-based evaluation.
watch_item: The framework is conceptually strong but will need clear practical validation of Π and robust criteria for detecting topological access to bifurcations in real flows.
paper_title: Coherence as Thermodynamic Organization: Toward a Non-Equilibrium Turbulence Theory
